name: Rodion Romanovitch Raskolnikov
description: A young, impoverished student struggling with severe financial and psychological issues. He is handsome but poorly dressed and often in a state of anxiety and indecision. Raskolnikov is haunted by an unnamed idea that he considers both terrifying and potentially transformative.

name: Alyona Ivanovna
description: An old, suspicious woman who runs a pawn shop in a dilapidated building. She is described as withered, sharp-eyed, and unfriendly, and she meticulously keeps track of her transactions and debts.

name: Lizaveta Ivanovna
description: Alyona's sister, who is not present during Raskolnikov's visit. She is mentioned but does not appear in the chapter.

name: Landlady
description: A woman who provides Raskolnikov with a room, meals, and services. She lives on the floor below him and is owed money by Raskolnikov, whom he fears encountering.

name: Drunkard
description: A drunk man encountered by Raskolnikov on the street who insults him, causing Raskolnikov to feel self-conscious about his appearance.

name: Retired Government Clerk
description: A man observed by Raskolnikov in the tavern, appearing agitated and occasionally drinking from his pot.

name: Semyon Zaharovitch Marmeladov
description: A former government clerk who has fallen into alcoholism and poverty. He is deeply remorseful for his actions and seeks understanding and forgiveness. His interactions with Raskolnikov reveal his complex relationship with his wife and daughter, highlighting themes of redemption and societal judgment.

name: Katerina Ivanovna
description: Marmeladov's wife, a former officer's daughter who is now ill and struggling to support her family. She is proud and quick-tempered, often lashing out at Marmeladov in frustration. Her condition worsens as the chapter progresses, adding to the family's distress.

name: Sofya Semyonovna Marmeladov
description: Marmeladov's daughter, who has turned to prostitution to support her family. Despite her circumstances, she shows compassion and care for her father and stepmother, embodying themes of sacrifice and resilience.

name: Andrey Semyonovitch Lebeziatnikov
description: A character mentioned by Marmeladov as someone who has beaten Katerina Ivanovna and caused further hardship for the family. His actions highlight the societal pressures and injustices faced by the family.

name: Amalia Fyodorovna Lippevechsel
description: The landlord who rents a room to Marmeladov's family. She is portrayed as strict and unforgiving, particularly towards Sonia, emphasizing the societal stigma surrounding prostitution.

name: Nastasya Nikiforovna
description: The cook and servant at Raskolnikov's residence. She is talkative and often intrusive, bringing him food and engaging him in conversation despite his apparent discomfort.

name: Praskovya Pavlovna
description: Raskolnikov's landlady who threatens to report him to the police for non-payment of rent and refusal to leave the premises.

name: Avdotya Romanovna
description: Raskolnikov's sister who has been working as a governess and recently endured hardships at the Svidrigaïlovs' house. She is engaged to Pyotr Petrovitch Luzhin, which offers financial relief to the family.

name: Pyotr Petrovitch Luzhin
description: A wealthy and ambitious man who is engaged to Dounia. He is described as practical, somewhat conceited, and interested in marrying a woman of good reputation who has experienced poverty.

name: Pulcheria Alexandrovna
description: Raskolnikov's mother, who wrote the letter informing him of Dounia's engagement. She is portrayed as loving but possibly manipulative, trying to convince Raskolnikov that the marriage is for his benefit. Her character is only mentioned through Raskolnikov's thoughts, but her influence is significant in shaping his current emotional state.

name: Policeman
description: A constable who intervenes when Raskolnikov confronts a gentleman who is attempting to take advantage of a drunken girl. The policeman attempts to help the girl but is ultimately thwarted by Raskolnikov's decision to abandon her. His character highlights the broader societal issues Raskolnikov is grappling with.

name: Dmitri Prokofitch Razumihin
description: Raskolnikov's old university friend, whom he briefly considers visiting but ultimately forgets about. Razumihin is described as a good-natured and intelligent individual, representing a potential source of support and understanding for Raskolnikov.

name: Mikolka
description: A character from Raskolnikov's dream, a drunkard who cruelly beats a weak horse to death. His actions symbolize the violence and cruelty that Raskolnikov is considering.

name: Pokorev
description: A student who mentions Alyona Ivanovna to Raskolnikov in a tavern, discussing her wealth and mistreatment of her sister Lizaveta. His conversation sparks Raskolnikov's thoughts about the morality of robbing Alyona.

name: The Porter
description: A minor character whose room Raskolnikov enters to steal an axe when he cannot retrieve it from the kitchen.

name: Koch
description: A visitor who arrives at Alyona's apartment after the murders, adding tension to the scene as he tries to gain entry.

name: Young Man
description: Another visitor who arrives with Koch and deduces that someone is inside the apartment, further complicating Raskolnikov's escape.

name: Porter
description: A man who delivers the summons from the police station to Raskolnikov. He is observant and notices Raskolnikov's unusual state but does not question him further.

name: Head Clerk
description: An official at the police station who handles Raskolnikov's summons for debt recovery. He is dismissive of Raskolnikov's condition and treats him with contempt.

name: Ilya Petrovitch
description: A stern and aggressive official at the police station who interrogates Raskolnikov and shows no sympathy for his condition. He is quick to anger and dismisses Raskolnikov's explanations.

name: Nikodim Fomitch
description: A more understanding official at the police station who tries to mediate between Raskolnikov and the Assistant Superintendent. He shows some concern for Raskolnikov's health but ultimately allows him to leave without further questioning.

name: Zametov
description: A police clerk who visited Raskolnikov's room during his illness. He is mentioned as a figure of authority and potential threat.

name: Messenger
description: A young man who delivers a remittance from Raskolnikov's mother. He is described as inquisitive and professional.

name: Afanasy Ivanovitch Vahrushin
description: A person who facilitated the remittance from Raskolnikov's mother. He is mentioned as a significant figure in Raskolnikov's life.

name: Dr. Zossimov
description: A physician attending to Raskolnikov, Zossimov is characterized as self-important and somewhat tedious, despite his professional competence. He is skeptical of Razumihin's arguments regarding Nikolay's innocence and the legal proceedings.

name: Nikolay Dementyev
description: Accused of the murder of Alyona Ivanovna and her sister Lizaveta, Nikolay is described as a painter who found jewelry and lied about it, leading to his arrest and attempted suicide. Razumihin believes in his innocence.

name: Afrosinya
description: A woman who attempts suicide by jumping into the canal. She is rescued by a policeman and recognized by a passerby.

name: Polenka
description: Marmeladov's eldest daughter, who runs after Raskolnikov to give a message from Sonia. She is described as a child of ten who understands her mother's needs and tries to help.

name: Porfiry Petrovitch
description: A detective handling a murder investigation. Razumihin mentions that Porfiry is eager to meet Raskolnikov.

name: Unknown Man
description: A man who follows Sofya Semyonovna after she leaves Raskolnikov's apartment, intrigued by her mention of Raskolnikov. He learns that she lives nearby and decides to investigate further.

name: Nikolay
description: A minor character mentioned by Porfiry Petrovitch, who is suspected of involvement in a crime. Razumihin defends his innocence.

name: Arkady Ivanovitch Svidrigailov
description: Introduced at the end of the chapter, this stranger watches Raskolnikov closely after he wakes from a nightmare. His presence adds an ominous and unsettling element to the conclusion of the chapter.

name: Marfa Petrovna
description: Svidrigaïlov's deceased wife, whose ghost he claims to have seen multiple times since her death. She is also mentioned in the context of her will, which includes a bequest to Avdotya Romanovna.

name: The man from underground
description: A visitor who informs Porfiry about Raskolnikov's inquiries about the flat and blood stains. His presence and revelations provide crucial context for Raskolnikov's situation and contribute to the resolution of the immediate crisis.

name: Amalia Ivanovna
description: Amalia Ivanovna is the landlady of the apartment where Katerina Ivanovna and her family reside. She is portrayed as a figure of authority and pride, often clashing with Katerina Ivanovna over the management of the household and the conduct of the dinner. Her interactions with Katerina Ivanovna are marked by mutual disrespect and escalating conflict.

name: Katia
description: A young woman who sings and performs for Svidrigaïlov in the tavern. She is paid and leaves after performing.

name: Philip
description: A waiter at the tavern who serves Svidrigaïlov and others. He is described as obsequious and friendly with Svidrigaïlov.

name: Kapernaumov children
description: Four children under Sonia's care who are present during Svidrigaïlov's visit but quickly leave in terror.

name: Fiancée's parents
description: The parents of Svidrigaïlov's fiancée, who receive a large sum of money from him and are surprised by his midnight visit.

name: Fiancée
description: Svidrigaïlov's fiancée who receives fifteen thousand roubles from him and is left in a state of excitement and confusion after his visit.

name: Achilles
description: A gatekeeper at a large house who encounters Svidrigaïlov and witnesses his suicide attempt.

name: Young girl
description: A neglected child found by Svidrigaïlov in his hotel room, who falls asleep after he helps her. She appears to Svidrigaïlov in a disturbing dream.
